Install for Free Now

Like You, We Were Tired of the Tedium

We are data enthusiasts and heavy users of productivity tools. For countless days and nights, needing to get data from web pages into Excel, we were tormented by broken formatting, hidden `<div>` tables, and slow extensions. We believed there had to be a better way. And so, 'Table Copy' was born. It's not bloated software, just a pure, fast, and focused tool designed to solve one problem: elegantly copying web tables.

3-Second Install, Use Forever

1

Press and Hold the Button

Click and hold the green 'Table Copy' button with your left mouse button.

2

Drag to Your Bookmarks Bar

Table Copy

Crucial Step: Drag the button to your browser's 'Bookmarks Bar' or 'Favorites Bar', then release the mouse.

3

Done!

Now, on any page with a table, just click this bookmark to start!

Note: This bookmarklet must be installed and used on a desktop browser.

One Tool for All Your Needs

Smart Structure Detection

Supports not only traditional `<table>` elements but also intelligently recognizes modern tables built with `<div>` layouts (based on ARIA standards).

Perfect One-Click Copy

Our unique Rich Text (HTML) copy feature writes the table structure to the clipboard, ensuring a perfect, format-preserving paste into Excel, WPS, or Notion.

Flexible Export Options

Copy as Rich Text, TSV, CSV, or JSON. Export directly to a CSV file (perfect for Excel) or even copy the table's raw HTML source code to meet all your needs.

Lightweight & Secure

It's just a bookmarklet. No installation, no background processes, ready when you are. All operations are performed locally in your browser. We never see, send, or store any of your data.

Export as Picture

Save the table as a PNG image with one click. Perfect for sharing in presentations, reports, or on social media. What you see is what you get.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Absolutely safe. Table Copy is a 100% client-side tool. All data recognition and processing happens locally in your browser. Nothing is ever sent to or stored on any server.

It's a 'bookmarklet,' which is much lighter than an extension. No installation from an app store, no background resource usage. Click to use, and it's gone when you're done. Of course, this also means it can't perform complex background tasks like scheduled scraping, which extensions can.

It supports the vast majority of tables using standard `<table>` tags or ARIA-compliant `<div>` structures. For pages built with extremely complex or non-standard frontend frameworks, it might not work perfectly. We are continuously improving the algorithm.

Yes, the current bookmarklet will always be free. We believe good tools should be widely accessible. In the future, we might release a more powerful paid browser extension (e.g., with multi-page scraping, scheduled tasks), but the core functionality you see today will always be free.
